finding_info.title: Ensure AppArmor is enabled
finding_info.desc: Linux security module (LSM) that provides mandatory access control (MAC) for applications. Strongly increases security by restricting applications to the bare minimum, follows the least privilege principle. Poorly written or missing AppArmor profiles can break applications that require access to files, network sockets, or devices not covered by the default profile.

remediation.desc: Install AppArmor and enable in bootloader with `apparmor=1 security=apparmor`, reboot, then slowly enforce profiles ensuring it does not break anything.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "Acquire::http::AllowRedirect" = "false"
finding_info.desc: Disabling HTTP redirects prevents man-in-the-middle attacks that could redirect package downloads to malicious servers.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "APT::Get::AllowUnauthenticated" = "false"
finding_info.desc: Blocks installation of packages without proper authentication.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "APT::Periodic::AutocleanInterval" = "7"
finding_info.desc: Automatically cleans package cache every 7 days, reducing disk space usage and potential stale package vulnerabilities.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "APT::Get::AutomaticRemove" = "true"
finding_info.desc: Automatically removes orphaned packages that are no longer needed, reducing the number of installed packages and the attack surface.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "APT::Install-Recommends" = "false"

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "APT::Install-Suggests" = "false"
finding_info.desc: Prevents automatic installation of suggested packages, minimizing attack surface.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories" = "false"
finding_info.desc: Blocks use of repositories without valid cryptographic signatures, preventing installation of tampered packages.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "Acquire::AllowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories" = "false"
finding_info.desc: Prevents downgrading a previously authenticated repository to an insecure one, blocking a potential supply chain attack vector.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "APT::Sandbox::Seccomp" = "true"
finding_info.desc: Enables Seccomp sandboxing for package management, providing additional process isolation.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "Unattended-Upgrade::Remove-Unused-Dependencies" = "true"
finding_info.desc: Automatically removes unused dependencies, minimizing attack surface.

finding_info.title: Ensure apt is configured with "Unattended-Upgrade::Remove-Unused-Kernel-Packages" = "true"
finding_info.desc: Automatically removes unused kernel packages, minimizing attack surface.

finding_info.title: Ensure "auditd" is running
finding_info.desc: Kernel-level subsystem that provides detailed logging and monitoring of system activities. Allows detection of attacks. Without auditd running, kernel-emitted security events go unrecorded. Audit logging adds disk I/O and CPU overhead; on busy systems, audit logs can grow rapidly and consume significant disk space, make sure to have a dedicated partition.

remediation.desc: Install and enable: "systemctl enable --now auditd". Verify with "systemctl status auditd".

finding_info.title: Ensure that audit is configured with "disk_full_action" = "HALT"
finding_info.desc: Halting the system when audit disk is full prevents an attacker from evading detection by filling up audit storage. Only apply in security critical environments, where it is more important than availability.

remediation.desc: Set "disk_full_action = HALT" in "/etc/audit/auditd.conf" and "systemctl restart auditd".

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rules are immutable
finding_info.desc: Immutable audit rules prevent attackers from disabling or modifying audit logging to cover their tracks. Once set, audit rules cannot be changed without a system reboot, which may block legitimate rule updates during system maintenance or testing.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker containers are not started with "--privileged" flag
finding_info.desc: Privileged containers have full access to the host system, effectively disabling all security isolation and allowing container escape to root on the host.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker containers capabilities are dropped
finding_info.desc: Dropping Linux capabilities reduces the kernel attack surface available to a compromised container, limiting the damage an attacker can do if they gain code execution. May break containers that require specific capabilities (e.g. NET_BIND_SERVICE for binding to low ports, SYS_PTRACE for debugging, NET_RAW for raw sockets).

finding_info.title: Ensure docker containers are running with a user
finding_info.desc: Containers running as root inside the namespace can exploit any kernel bug, capability loophole, or shared mount to escape the container. Running as a non-root UID forces an attacker to find an additional escalation primitive first. Limit impact of a container process compromise and follow principle of least privilege.

remediation.desc: Set `USER` in the Dockerfile to a non-root UID, or pass `--user <uid>` at run time.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker mount point "/var/lib/docker" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate filesystem for /var/lib/containers lets the operator apply hardened mount options (e.g. nodev, quotas) to container storage and prevents a runaway container from filling the root filesystem and breaking host services.

remediation.desc: Mount /var/lib/containers as a dedicated filesystem in /etc/fstab, consider `nodev` and disk quotas.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker network traffic is restricted between containers on the default bridge
finding_info.desc: By default all containers on the default bridge can communicate freely, which allows lateral movement if one container is compromised. Restricting inter-container communication limits blast radius. Breaks legitimate inter-container communication on the default bridge network; use custom networks with explicit links if containers need to communicate.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker logging level is set to info
finding_info.desc: Setting the log level to info ensures that security-relevant events are captured without excessive noise, enabling effective incident detection and forensic analysis.

remediation.desc: In "/etc/docker/daemon.json" add `{"log-level": "info"}`, or start the daemon with `--no-new-privileges` flag.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker is allowed to make changes to iptables
finding_info.desc: Docker manages container networking by inserting iptables rules. Disabling this breaks port publishing and network isolation, leaving containers exposed or unreachable.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker does not allow insecure registry
finding_info.desc: Insecure registries allow unencrypted and unauthenticated communication, exposing image pulls and pushes to man-in-the-middle attacks and credential theft.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker storage driver is not aufs
finding_info.desc: The aufs storage driver is deprecated and has known security issues including incomplete layer isolation. Using a supported driver reduces the risk of container filesystem leaks.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker storage options "dm.basesize" are not set
finding_info.desc: Setting dm.basesize caps the root filesystem size of new containers using the devicemapper driver. Growing it beyond the default increases disk consumption per container and can exhaust the thin-pool. Most workloads do not need to change it.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker uses an authorization plugin
finding_info.desc: Without an authorization plugin, any user with access to the Docker daemon can execute any Docker command, including privileged operations that could compromise the host. Some attackers use containers to evade security tools like EDR.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker containers cannot acquire new privileges
finding_info.desc: Set no-new-privileges by default for new containers. Prevents processes inside containers from gaining additional privileges via setuid/setgid binaries or filesystem capabilities. Breaks containers that rely on privilege escalation (e.g. some init systems, sudo within containers).

remediation.desc: In "/etc/docker/daemon.json" add `{"no-new-privileges": true}`, or start the daemon with `--no-new-privileges` flag.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker builtin seccomp profile is used
finding_info.desc: Use the builtin seccomp Docker profile to ensure some system calls are restricted within containers.

remediation.desc: In "/etc/docker/daemon.json" remove `{"seccomp-profile": "unconfined"}`, or start the daemon without `--seccomp-profile unconfined` flag.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker live restore is enabled
finding_info.desc: Live restore keeps containers running during daemon downtime, preventing denial of service during Docker daemon updates or restarts.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker userland proxy is disabled
finding_info.desc: The userland proxy bypasses iptables filtering rules, which means network-based security policies are not enforced on proxied traffic, weakening network segmentation. Disabling it may break port publishing on systems where the kernel does not support hairpin NAT or when using the default bridge network on some platforms.

remediation.desc: In "/etc/docker/daemon.json" remove `{"userlad-proxy": false}`, or start the daemon without `--userlad-proxy false` flag.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker runs without experimental features
finding_info.desc: Experimental features are not fully tested and may contain security vulnerabilities or unexpected behaviors that could be exploited to compromise the Docker host.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker service file is owned by root
finding_info.desc: If the Docker service file is not owned by root, a non-privileged user could modify it to escalate privileges or alter daemon startup behavior.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker swarm is disabled if not needed
finding_info.desc: Docker Swarm mode exposes additional attack surface including a distributed key-value store and overlay networking. Disabling it when not needed reduces the risk of cluster-level compromise.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker group is empty
finding_info.desc: Membership in the docker group grants the ability to interact with the Docker socket, which effectively provides root-equivalent access to the host system.

finding_info.title: Ensure docker containers root filesystem is mounted as read-only
finding_info.desc: Read-only root filesystems prevent attackers from writing malicious binaries, modifying system files, or tampering with container contents after compromise. Forces explicit volume mounts for writable data, improving security posture and making containers more immutable.

remediation.desc: Start containers with `--read-only` flag, or set `"ReadonlyRootfs": true` in container config. Use `--tmpfs` or named volumes for directories that need write access.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker daemon is present
finding_info.desc: Auditing the Docker daemon binary ensures all invocations are logged, enabling detection of unauthorized Docker usage or tampering with the daemon executable.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker run files and directories is present
finding_info.desc: Auditing the containerd runtime directory detects unauthorized modifications to runtime state, which could indicate container escape attempts or runtime tampering.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker var lib files and directories is present
finding_info.desc: The /var/lib/docker directory contains container images, volumes, and layer data. Auditing it detects unauthorized access or modification of container storage.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker etc files and directories is present
finding_info.desc: Auditing the /etc/docker directory detects unauthorized changes to Docker configuration files and TLS certificates, which could be used to weaken daemon security.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker etc default file is present
finding_info.desc: Auditing the /etc/default/docker file detects unauthorized changes to Docker daemon environment variables and startup options that could weaken security.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker etc daemon file is present
finding_info.desc: Auditing the daemon.json configuration file provides a trail of any changes to Docker daemon settings, enabling detection of unauthorized security configuration modifications.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker etc containerd config file is present
finding_info.desc: Auditing the containerd configuration file detects unauthorized changes to the container runtime, which could disable security features like seccomp or AppArmor profiles.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker sysconfig file is present
finding_info.desc: Auditing the sysconfig docker file detects unauthorized changes to Docker daemon options on RHEL/CentOS systems, which could introduce insecure configurations.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker containerd bin is present
finding_info.desc: Auditing the containerd binary detects unauthorized replacement or modification of the container runtime, which could be used to bypass container isolation.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for docker runc bin is present
finding_info.desc: Auditing the runc binary detects unauthorized replacement or modification of the low-level container runtime.

finding_info.title: Ensure CopyFail (CVE-2026-31431) is mitigated
finding_info.desc: CVE-2026-31431, CopyFail, is a local privilege escalation (LPE), affecting every Linux distribution using Linux kernel versions between 4.14 and 6.19.12. The mitigation is to prohibits kernel modules "algif_aead" from starting.

finding_info.title: Ensure no automatic logon to the system via a GUI is possible
finding_info.desc: Automatic GUI login bypasses authentication, allowing anyone with physical access to gain immediate access to the system.

findings.message: failed to read gdm configuration: No such file or directory (os error 2)

remediation.desc: Set `AutomaticLoginEnable=false` (and remove `AutomaticLogin=`) in /etc/gdm3/custom.conf or /etc/gdm/custom.conf, then restart gdm.

finding_info.title: Ensure group shadow file is empty or missing
finding_info.desc: Group passwords stored in /etc/gshadow let any holder switch into the group via `newgrp`, expanding lateral movement. Modern systems do not need group passwords and the file should be empty or absent so this attack vector does not exist.

remediation.desc: Remove or empty "/etc/gshadow", ensure no group has a password by clearing the second field of each line via `gpasswd -r <group>`.

finding_info.title: Ensure no group has a password set
finding_info.desc: A password in /etc/group lets any user with that password assume the group's privileges via `newgrp`, bypassing the membership list, turning the group hash into a shared lateral-movement credential as soon as it leaks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that only root has GID 0
finding_info.desc: A second group with GID 0 is privilege-equivalent to `root` for filesystem and IPC ACLs. An attacker who creates one or who pivots into membership gains root-level group access without ever being root.

remediation.desc: Remove or renumber any non-`root` group with GID 0 via `groupmod -g <new-gid> <name>`, investigate how it was created.

finding_info.title: Ensure no duplicate GIDs exist
finding_info.desc: Two group names sharing one GID makes audit logs and ACL decisions ambiguous: a file owned by GID X cannot be reliably attributed to one group, hiding privilege relationships and complicating forensics.

finding_info.title: Ensure no duplicate group names exist
finding_info.desc: Duplicate group names indicate manual editing of "/etc/group" or a corrupt name service.

remediation.desc: Edit "/etc/group" (with `vigr`) to remove or rename the duplicate.

finding_info.title: Ensure "shadow" group is empty
finding_info.desc: Members of the `shadow` group can read "/etc/shadow" and crack account's password hash. Membership should be empty so no non-root account holds that capability.

remediation.desc: Remove all members from the `shadow` group via `gpasswd -d <user> shadow`.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/group" file owner is "root:root"
finding_info.desc: If "/etc/group" is owned by a non-root user, that user can edit group membership and silently grant themselves any group's privileges, including `wheel`, `sudo`, or `docker`, each of which leads to root.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/group" file permissions are "644"
finding_info.desc: Permissions wider than 0644 let unprivileged users modify group membership. Tighter than 0644 breaks userland tools that expect to read group names. 0644 is the only safe value.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/gshadow" file owner is "root:root" or file is missing
finding_info.desc: Wrong ownershoip of "/etc/gshadow" leaks group password hashes (when present) for offline cracking and exposes sensitive group elevation policy.

remediation.desc:
On Debian: `chown root:shadow /etc/gshadow`
On other distros: `chown root:root /etc/gshadow`.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/gshadow" file permissions are set or file is missing
finding_info.desc: World- or group-readable "/etc/gshadow" leaks group password hashes (when present) for offline cracking and exposes sensitive group elevation policy.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/gshadow-" file owner is "root:root" or file is missing
finding_info.desc: "/etc/gshadow-" is the previous-generation backup of gshadow, if its ownership is wrong, an attacker can recover group hashes and policy from the backup that the live file no longer reveals.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/gshadow-" file permissions are set or file is missing
finding_info.desc: "/etc/gshadow-" is the previous-generation backup of gshadow, if its permissions are wrong, an attacker can recover group hashes and policy from the backup that the live file no longer reveals.

finding_info.title: Ensure that GRUB bootloader password is set
finding_info.desc: Setting a GRUB bootloader password prevents an attacker with physical access from editing kernel boot parameters (e.g., adding init=/bin/bash) to bypass authentication and gain root access. Even if the root fs is encrypted, an attacker could boot in recovery mode, and tamper with EFI or /boot partition, potentially enabling passphrase theft. Forgetting the GRUB password requires physical access with a live CD/USB to reset, potentially locking out legitimate administrators.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "slab_nomerge" is present
finding_info.desc: Disable slab merging, increasing the difficulty of heap exploit implied by "slub_debug=FZ", but having "slab_nomerge" explicitly declared can help prevent regressions where disabling of debugging features is desired but re-enabling of merging is not. Increases memory consumption as slabs cannot be merged, and may reduce allocation performance.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "slab_debug=FZ" is present
finding_info.desc: Enables front and end zone poisoning in slab allocator, helping detect memory corruption, buffer overflows, and use-after-free vulnerabilities by inserting canary values around memory allocations. Significant performance overhead due to extra memory usage and checks on every allocation/free.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "page_alloc.shuffle=1" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable the kernel page allocator to randomize free lists during early boot. Limits some data exfiltration and ROP attacks that rely on inferring sensitive data location, also improves performance by optimizing memory-side cache utilization. Needs CONFIG_SHUFFLE_PAGE_ALLOCATOR=y kernel build config too.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "init_on_alloc=1" is present
finding_info.desc: Zero memory at allocation time. Mitigates use-after-free exploits by erasing sensitive information in memory. Performance overhead from zeroing every allocation; impact varies by workload.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "init_on_free=1" is present
finding_info.desc: Zero memory at free time. Mitigates use-after-free exploits by erasing sensitive information in memory. Performance overhead from zeroing every freed page; impact varies by workload.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "pti=on" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable kernel page table isolation to harden against kernel ASLR (KASLR) bypasses, mitigates the Meltdown (CVE-2017-5754) CPU vulnerability. Performance overhead from additional TLB flushes on every kernel/userspace transition; impact varies by CPU and workload (up to 30% on some server workloads).

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "randomize_kstack_offset=on" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable randomization of the kernel stack offset on syscall entries. Hardens against memory corruption attacks due to increased entropy limits attacks relying on deterministic stack addresses or cross-syscall address exposure. Minor performance overhead from extra randomization on every syscall.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "vsyscall=none" is present
finding_info.desc: Disable vsyscalls to reduce attack surface as they have been replaced by vDSO vulnerable to ROP attacks as vsyscalls are located at fixed addresses in memory. Specific to x86_64 arch. Breaks very old binaries (pre-glibc 2.22) and some legacy applications that rely on vsyscalls.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "debugfs=off" is present
finding_info.desc: Restrict access to debugfs that can contain sensitive information. Breaks tools that rely on debugfs (e.g. some GPU drivers, perf tools, power management utilities, debugging tools).

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "oops=panic" is present
finding_info.desc: Force the kernel to panic on "oopses", can sometimes potentially indicate and thwart certain kernel exploitation attempts, also cause panics on machine check exceptions. Some bad drivers can cause harmless oopses which result in system crash.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "module.sig_enforce=1" is present
finding_info.desc: Require every kernel module to be signed before being loaded. Any module that is unsigned or signed with an invalid key cannot be loaded. Prevents all out-of-tree kernel modules (including DKMS) unless signed, this makes it harder to load a malicious module.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "lockdown=integrity" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable kernel lockdown to enforce security boundary between user and kernel space, enforces module signature verification kernel lockdown LSM can eliminate many methods that user space code could abuse for privilege escalation. Some applications may cease to work which rely on low-level access to either hardware or the kernel.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "mce=0" is present
finding_info.desc: Keeps the kernel from logging machine check exception (MCE) events that an attacker could correlate with covert side-channel work. Unnecessary for systems without ECC memory.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "kfence.sample_interval=100" is present
finding_info.desc: KFENCE detects heap out-of-bounds access, use-after-free, and invalid-free errors. Sampling interval is set to occur every 100 ms as per KSPP recommendation. Small performance and memory overhead from maintaining guard pages for sampled allocations.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "vdso32=0" is present
finding_info.desc: Disables the 32-bit vDSO, removing a small fixed-address ROP-friendly mapping from 64-bit processes that don't need it. Reduces predictable kernel-exposed addresses available to exploits. Breaks 32-bit applications that rely on vDSO for fast time-related syscalls (e.g. gettimeofday).

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "amd_iommu=force_isolation" is present
finding_info.desc: Forces AMD IOMMU into per-device isolation domains, blocking DMA attacks from peripherals (Thunderbolt, PCIe, FireWire) that would otherwise let a malicious or compromised device read/write arbitrary host memory.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "intel_iommu=on" is present
finding_info.desc: Enables Intel VT-d/IOMMU , blocking DMA attacks from peripherals (Thunderbolt, PCIe, FireWire) that would otherwise let a malicious or compromised device read/write arbitrary host memory.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "iommu=force" is present
finding_info.desc: Force-enable IOMMU , blocking DMA attacks from peripherals (Thunderbolt, PCIe, FireWire) that would otherwise let a malicious or compromised device read/write arbitrary host memory.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "iommu.passthrough=0" is present
finding_info.desc: Disable IOMMU passthrough so every DMA request goes through the IOMMU translation tables. Prevents devices from performing direct physical-memory reads and writes. Can reduce I/O performance, but the impact is small on modern hardware.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "iommu.strict=1" is present
finding_info.desc: Strict IOMMU mode flushes IOTLB entries immediately when DMA mappings are torn down, closing the window where a device could still access stale mappings after the driver believes it has revoked access. Performance overhead from frequent IOTLB flushes; impact varies by I/O workload.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "efi=disable_early_pci_dma" is present
finding_info.desc: Block PCI DMA during early EFI boot before the IOMMU is initialized. Without this, a malicious or compromised peripheral can perform DMA attacks during the boot window before IOMMU protection is active.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "random.trust_bootloader=off" is present
finding_info.desc: Do not trust entropy provided by the bootloader. A compromised or malicious bootloader could supply predictable seed values, weakening the kernel RNG from the start. May increase boot time.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "random.trust_cpu=off" is present
finding_info.desc: Do not trust CPU-provided entropy (e.g. RDRAND). A backdoored or flawed hardware RNG could produce predictable output, weakening all cryptographic operations that depend on the kernel RNG. May increase boot time.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "extra_latent_entropy" is present
finding_info.desc: Gather additional entropy from compiler-instrumented latent variables during early boot, seeding the kernel RNG with hard-to-predict state transitions. Strengthens cryptographic randomness on systems with limited hardware entropy sources. May increase boot time.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "ia32_emulation=0" is present
finding_info.desc: Disable 32-bit IA-32 emulation, removing hundreds of legacy 32-bit syscalls from the attack surface. 64-bit systems do not need it unless running legacy 32-bit binaries. Also simplifies security monitoring and application policy. All 32-bit binaries (e.g. Wine, Steam, legacy software) will no longer run.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "cfi=kcfi" is present
finding_info.desc: Disable FineIBT since it is weaker than pure KCFI.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "hardened_usercopy=1" is present
finding_info.desc: Refuse to copy data between kernel and user space if the destination/source is not a valid user buffer. Blocks a class of heap-based information leaks and overflows that rely on usercopy primitives. Performance overhead from additional bounds checking on every usercopy operation.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "remountsecure=3" is present
finding_info.desc: Re-mount all filesystems at boot with the strictest options: nodev, nosuid, and noexec for every mount point including /home. Prevents executable payloads on writable mounts. May break scripts, JIT-generated code, plugins, interpreters.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "mitigations=auto" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable all CPU vulnerability mitigations automatically. Protects against Spectre, Meltdown, MDS, TSX Async Abort, and other speculative-execution side-channel attacks. Performance overhead from all active mitigations; impact varies by CPU and workload (typically 5-30%).

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "mitigations=auto,nosmt" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable all CPU vulnerability mitigations and disable Simultaneous Multithreading. Provides maximum protection against cross-thread side-channel attacks like ForgeCache and ShadowClone. SMT/Hyper-Threading is disabled, reducing available logical CPUs. May significantly decrease system performance on multi-threaded tasks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "nosmt" is present
finding_info.desc: Disable Simultaneous Multithreading. SMT/Hyper-Threading is disabled, reducing available logical CPUs. May significantly decrease system performance on multi-threaded tasks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "spectre_v2=on" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable mitigation for the Spectre variant 2 vulnerability. Affects both Intel and AMD CPUs. Performance overhead from branch target injection mitigations (retpoline/IBRS); impact varies by CPU and workload (typically 5-20%).

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "spectre_bhi=on" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable mitigation for the Spectre branch history injection vulnerability. Affects both Intel and AMD CPUs. Performance overhead from branch history clearing on every syscall entry; impact varies by CPU and workload.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "spec_store_bypass_disable=on" is present
finding_info.desc: Unconditionally disable Speculative Store Bypass (SSB) on affected CPUs. Performance overhead from speculative store bypass mitigation; impact varies by CPU and workload.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "l1tf=full,force" is present
finding_info.desc: Unconditionally enable L1 Terminal Fault mitigation and disable SMT. Prevents information leakage from L1 cache via the Foreshadow side-channel attack. SMT/Hyper-Threading is disabled, reducing available logical CPUs. May significantly decrease system performance on multi-threaded tasks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "mds=full" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable full Microarchitectural Data Sampling mitigation. Clears CPU buffers before returning to user space to prevent side-channel data leakage across hyperthreads. Performance overhead from VERW instruction on every kernel exit; impact varies by CPU and workload.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "mds=full,nosm" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable full MDS mitigation and disable SMT for maximum protection against microarchitectural data sampling attacks. SMT/Hyper-Threading is disabled, reducing available logical CPUs. May significantly decrease system performance on multi-threaded tasks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "tsx=off" is present
finding_info.desc: Disable Intel TSX (Transactional Synchronization Extensions). TSX-based speculative execution creates side channels exploitable by TAA and other attacks. Breaks applications relying on hardware transactional memory (e.g. some databases, high-performance computing).

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "tsx_async_abort=full" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable full TSX Async Abort mitigation. Clears CPU buffers to prevent data leakage via the TSX side channel (TAA/CVE-2019-11135). Performance overhead from VERW instruction on every kernel exit.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "tsx_async_abort=full,nosmt" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable full TAA mitigation and disable SMT. Provides maximum protection against TSX Async Abort side-channel attacks. SMT/Hyper-Threading is disabled, reducing available logical CPUs. May significantly decrease system performance on multi-threaded tasks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "kvm.nx_huge_pages=force" is present
finding_info.desc: Force NX huge pages for KVM guests, mitigating the iTLB Multihit vulnerability (CVE-2019-19332) where a malicious guest can trigger machine check exceptions on hosts with certain CPU errata. May reduce KVM guest performance by forcing memory to use huge pages only when NX is not required.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "l1d_flush=on" is present
finding_info.desc: Flush the L1 data cache on VM entry to prevent cross-guest data leakage via the L1 cache side channel (CVE-2018-3640 / L1TF). Performance overhead from L1 cache flush on every VM entry; impact varies by VM workload frequency.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "mmio_stale_data=full" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable full MMIO stale data mitigation (CVE-2022-21123/21125/21127/24549). Clears CPU buffers to prevent data leakage from MMIO operations. Performance overhead from VERW instruction on VM entry/exit and kernel exit.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "mmio_stale_data=full,nosmt" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable full MMIO stale data mitigation and disable SMT. Maximum protection against Processor MMIO Stale Data vulnerabilities. SMT/Hyper-Threading is disabled, reducing available logical CPUs. May significantly decrease system performance on multi-threaded tasks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "retbleed=auto" is present
finding_info.desc: Automatically select Retbleed mitigation based on the CPU. Prevents speculative execution of return instructions from leaking data via the RetBleed side channel (CVE-2022-29900/29901). Performance overhead from return instruction mitigation; impact varies by CPU and workload.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "retbleed=auto,nosmt" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable automatic Retbleed mitigation and disable SMT. Maximum protection against Retbleed side-channel attacks. SMT/Hyper-Threading is disabled, reducing available logical CPUs. May significantly decrease system performance on multi-threaded tasks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "spec_rstack_overflow=safe-ret" is present
finding_info.desc: Mitigate Speculative Return Stack Overflow (CVE-2022-28693/29392/29393/29394). Use safe-ret training sequences to prevent guest-to-host and guest-to-guest speculation via the return address predictor. Performance overhead from safe-ret training on every function return.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "gather_data_sampling=force" is present
finding_info.desc: Force-enable Gather Data Sampling mitigation (CVE-2022-40982). Prevents data leakage via the AVX2 gather instruction side channel. Performance overhead for AVX2-heavy workloads that use gather instructions.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "reg_file_data_sampling=on" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable Register File Data Sampling mitigation (CVE-2023-28692 / Downfall). Prevents data leakage from architectural register file state via speculative execution side channels. Performance overhead on Intel CPUs from additional mitigation steps on context switches.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "spectre_v2_user=on" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable Spectre v2 user-space mitigation unconditionally. Protects user-space processes from cross-process Spectre v2 attacks (indirect branch injection). Performance overhead from STIBP/IBPB on context switches; impact varies by CPU and workload (typically 5-15%).

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "srbds=auto,nosmt" is present
finding_info.desc: Enable SRBDS mitigation and disable SMT. Protects against Special Register Buffer Data Sampling (CVE-2020-0548) which leaks data from special registers via a side channel. SMT/Hyper-Threading is disabled, reducing available logical CPUs. May significantly decrease system performance on multi-threaded tasks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "loglevel=0" is present
finding_info.desc: Prevent sensitive kernel information leaks in the console during boot.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "quiet" is present
finding_info.desc: Prevent sensitive kernel information leaks in the console during boot.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel flag "hash_pointers=always" is present
finding_info.desc: Hash all kernel pointers printed via printk and other output paths. Prevents kernel address leaks that aid exploitation via dmesg, /proc/kallsyms, and other interfaces.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "ENCRYPT_METHOD" = "YESCRYPT"
finding_info.desc: Use stronger hashing algorithms.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "YESCRYPT_COST_FACTOR" >= 5
finding_info.desc: A higher cost factor multiplies the work an attacker must spend per guess in offline cracking. With yescrypt now consumed by PAM, this directly raises the bar for password cracking from any leaked /etc/shadow. Higher cost factors increase CPU time for password hashing during login and password changes, which may cause noticeable delays on systems with many concurrent logins.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs -1 < "PASS_MAX_DAYS" <= 365
finding_info.desc: Forcing periodic password rotation limits the value of any single leaked credential: an attacker who steals a hash today, and if he is able to crack it, loses access once it expires. Combined with strong hashing, it bounds the window of unauthorized use.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "PASS_MIN_DAYS" >= 1
finding_info.desc: Without a minimum age, a user forced to change their password can rotate it through history many times and return to the original, bypassing reuse-prevention policy.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "PASS_WARN_AGE" >= 7
finding_info.desc: Warning users before passwords expire prevents last-minute panicked rotations to weak passwords.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "SYSLOG_SU_ENAB" = "yes"
finding_info.desc: Without `SYSLOG_SU_ENAB`, `su` invocations bypass syslog, making privilege escalations between accounts effectively invisible to centralized logging and SIEM detections.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "SYSLOG_SG_ENAB" = "yes"
finding_info.desc: Without `SYSLOG_SG_ENAB`, `sg`/`newgrp` group switches are not syslogged, hiding lateral access to group-owned resources from incident-response timelines.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "UMASK" = "077"
finding_info.desc: A default UMASK of 077 makes new files readable only by their owner. Prevent potential information leak when creating files.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "LOGIN_RETRIES" <= 3
finding_info.desc: Maximum number of login retries in case of bad password. This will most likely be overridden by PAM, since the default pam_unix module has its own built in of 3 retries. However, this is a safe fallback in case you are using an authentication module that does not enforce PAM_MAXTRIES.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "LOGIN_TIMEOUT" <= 60
finding_info.desc: An unbounded login timeout lets an attacker hold a login prompt open indefinitely, consuming a TTY slot.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "FAILLOG_ENAB" = "yes"
finding_info.desc: Recording failed login attempts to /var/log/faillog lets administrators and tools reconstruct brute-force or credential-stuffing campaigns. Without it, failed attempts leave no trace on disk. Replaced by pam_faillock.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "LOG_OK_LOGINS" = "yes"
finding_info.desc: Logging successful logins creates an audit trail of who accessed the system and when, enabling detection of unauthorized account use and supporting incident-response timelines.

finding_info.title: Ensure that login.defs "LOG_UNKFAIL_ENAB" = "no"
finding_info.desc: Do not log unknown usernames when login failures are recorded. Logging unknown usernames is an issue if a user enter his password instead of his username.

finding_info.title: Ensure "scudo" hardened malloc is used system wide
finding_info.desc: Scudo hardened allocators deterministically detect or mitigate common heap-corruption primitives: use-after-free, double-free, out-of-bounds writes, type confusion across slabs; that the default glibc allocator leaves exploitable. Without one, heap bugs in any setuid or network-facing process are far easier to weaponize. Defense-in-depth to prevent bug exploitation.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/modprobe.d" directory is owned by root
finding_info.desc: /etc/modprobe.d holds the module loading policy (blacklist, install, options) that every other module check relies on, non-root ownership lets that user rewrite the policy, re-enable disabled modules or inject module options, allowing for local privilege escalation.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/modprobe.d" directory permissions is 755 or stricter
finding_info.desc: /etc/modprobe.d holds the module loading policy, group or world writable permissions let unprivileged users drop a config file to override blacklists, re-enable disabled modules or inject module options, allowing for local privilege escalation.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/modprobe.d" files are owned by root
finding_info.desc: Modprobe reads every ".conf" file in /etc/modprobe.d to build the module loading policy, a config file owned by a non-root user lets that user blacklist, re-enable or change options of any module, allowing for local privilege escalation.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/modprobe.d" files permissions are 644 or stricter
finding_info.desc: Modprobe reads every ".conf" file in /etc/modprobe.d to build the module loading policy, a writable config file lets unprivileged users blacklist, re-enable or change options of any module, allowing for local privilege escalation.

finding_info.title: Ensure that kernel module "amd76x_edac" is blacklisted
finding_info.desc: Prevents the kernel module "amd76x_edac" from auto-loading on hardware probe or subsystem request, reducing the attack surface from unused modules that could contain exploitable vulnerabilities. The module remains manually loadable by root if needed. Legacy AMD 76x EDAC memory-error reporting driver.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount point "/boot" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate /boot partition allows it to be mounted read-only after boot, preventing attackers from modifying kernel or bootloader files.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount point "/tmp" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate /tmp filesystem prevents temporary file abuse from filling the root partition, protecting from potential DOS, and allows restrictive mount options like noexec.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount point "/home" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate /home partition allows filesystem-specific security options like noexec.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount point "/var" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate /var partition prevents variable data from filling the root filesystem and allows restrictive mount options like noexec.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount point "/var/log" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate /var/log partition ensures audit logs survive a full root filesystem and allows restrictive mount options.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount point "/var/log/audit" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate /var/log/audit partition ensures audit logs survive disk exhaustion attacks and allows restrictive mount options.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount point "/var/tmp" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate /var/tmp partition isolates large temporary files from /tmp and allows restrictive mount options.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount point "/dev/shm" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate /dev/shm mount allows restrictive options to prevent shared-memory abuse.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount option "nodev" is set for "/dev/shm"
finding_info.desc: Prevent device node creation on /dev/shm, blocking attackers from creating block devices to bypass filesystem access controls.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount option "nodev" is set for "/boot"
finding_info.desc: Prevent device node creation on /boot, blocking attackers from creating block devices to bypass filesystem access controls.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount option "nosuid" is set for "/boot"
finding_info.desc: Ignore SUID bits on /boot, preventing attackers from exploiting setuid binaries.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount option "noexec" is set for "/boot"
finding_info.desc: Prevent direct execution of binaries on /boot, blocking attackers from running malicious code placed in the boot partition.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount option "noauto" is set for "/boot"
finding_info.desc: Require explicit mounting of /boot, reducing the window during which attackers can modify boot files. /boot is only needed during kernel updates.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount option "nosuid" is set for "/dev/shm"
finding_info.desc: Ignore SUID bits on /dev/shm, preventing attackers from exploiting setuid binaries.

finding_info.title: Ensure mount option "noexec" is set for "/dev/shm"
finding_info.desc: Prevent execution of binaries on /dev/shm, blocking attackers from running exploits from shared memory. This could be used to bypass AV and EDR that scan files created on disk but may ignore files created in shared memory.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/" partition is encrypted with LUKS
finding_info.desc: LUKS full disk encryption protects data at rest against physical access, theft, or improper disposal of storage media. Without it, an attacker with physical access to the disk can read sensitive data directly, bypassing all filesystem permissions and access controls. This is acceptable to leave unencrypted under specific context, for example a VM running on an hypervisor with an encrypted host disk is not an issue, an host with no sensitive data, or a diskless setup.

remediation.desc: Re-encrypting an existing partition usually requires a backup and a reinstall, follow your distribution documentation to setup LUKS.

finding_info.title: Ensure nginx server_tokens is set to off
finding_info.desc: The server_tokens directive controls whether nginx sends its version number in error pages and the Server response header. This is not directly a security measure as it offer no protection against attacks, but prevent information leakage about update management that could reflect a company security and operational posture.

remediation.desc: Add "server_tokens off;" in the http block.

finding_info.title: Ensure nginx X-Frame-Options header is set
finding_info.desc: The X-Frame-Options header prevents clickjacking attacks by controlling whether the page can be embedded in frames.

remediation.desc: Add 'add_header X-Frame-Options "DENY" always;' in the http or server block.

finding_info.title: Ensure nginx X-Content-Type-Options header is set
finding_info.desc: The X-Content-Type-Options header prevents MIME type sniffing, which can lead to XSS attacks.

remediation.desc: Add 'add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;' in the http or server block.

finding_info.title: Ensure nginx Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header is set
finding_info.desc: HSTS tells browsers to only connect over HTTPS, preventing protocol downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking.

remediation.desc: Add 'add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;' in the http or server block.

finding_info.title: Ensure nginx HTTP to HTTPS redirect is configured
finding_info.desc: An HTTP to HTTPS redirect ensures all traffic is encrypted. Without it, users may inadvertently send data over unencrypted connections.

remediation.desc: Add a server block listening on port 80 with 'return 301 https://$host$request_uri;'.

finding_info.title: Ensure PAM service "passwd" has rule "account required pam_unix"
finding_info.desc: Without `pam_unix` enforcing account validity on password changes, expired or locked accounts could still rotate credentials and regain interactive access, undermining account-lifecycle controls.

finding_info.title: Ensure PAM service "passwd" has rule "password required pam_pwquality"
finding_info.desc: Enforce password policy.

finding_info.title: Ensure PAM service "su" has rule "auth required pam_wheel"
finding_info.desc: Without `pam_wheel` gating `su`, any compromised local account can attempt root password attacks. Restricting `su` to a single privileged group narrows the privilege-escalation path and aids audit attribution.

remediation.desc: Add "auth required pam_wheel.so use_uid" to "/etc/pam.d/su" and add the intended admins to the `wheel` group.

finding_info.title: Ensure PAM service "login" has rule "auth required pam_faillock"
finding_info.desc: Without `pam_faillock` locking accounts after repeated failed logins, an attacker with console or terminal access can brute-force passwords. Legitimate users who mistype their password too many times will have their account locked out, requiring administrator intervention to unlock.

remediation.desc: Add "auth required pam_faillock.so preauth" and "auth [default=die] pam_faillock.so authfail" entries to "/etc/pam.d/login" (or common-auth).

finding_info.title: Ensure PAM service "login" has rule "auth optional pam_faildelay"
finding_info.desc: `pam_faildelay` adds a randomized pause after failed authentications, defeating timing side channels that distinguish unknown user from wrong password. Adds latency to failed login attempts, which may be noticeable in automated login scripts or rapid retry scenarios.

finding_info.title: Ensure podman containers are not started with "--privileged" flag
finding_info.desc: Privileged containers have full access to the host system, effectively disabling all security isolation (seccomp/AppArmor/SELinux) and allowing container escape to root on the host.

remediation.desc: Run containers without `--privileged`. If specific capabilities or devices are needed, grant them individually via `--cap-add`/`--device`.

finding_info.title: Ensure podman containers capabilities are dropped
finding_info.desc: Dropping Linux capabilities reduces the kernel attack surface available to a compromised container, limiting the damage an attacker can do if they gain code execution. May break containers that require specific capabilities (e.g. NET_BIND_SERVICE for binding to low ports, SYS_PTRACE for debugging, NET_RAW for raw sockets).

finding_info.title: Ensure podman containers are started with a user
finding_info.desc: Containers running as root inside the namespace can exploit any kernel bug, capability loophole, or shared mount to escape the container. Running as a non-root UID forces an attacker to find an additional escalation primitive first. Limit impact of a container process compromise and follow principle of least privilege.

remediation.desc: Set `USER` in the Dockerfile to a non-root UID, or pass `--user <uid>` at run time.

finding_info.title: Ensure podman mount point "/var/lib/containers" exist
finding_info.desc: A separate filesystem for /var/lib/containers lets the operator apply hardened mount options (e.g. nodev, quotas) to container storage and prevents a runaway container from filling the root filesystem and breaking host services.

remediation.desc: Mount /var/lib/containers as a dedicated filesystem in /etc/fstab, consider `nodev` and disk quotas.

finding_info.title: Ensure apparmor is enabled for podman
finding_info.desc: AppArmor confines container processes via mandatory access control. With it disabled, a compromised container relies only on namespaces and capabilities for isolation, removing a defence-in-depth layer that has historically blocked container escapes.

remediation.desc: Install and enable AppArmor host-side, ensure podman picks up the default container profile.

finding_info.title: Ensure podman containers are started with an apparmor profile
finding_info.desc: Even with AppArmor enabled host-side, a container started with `--security-opt apparmor=unconfined` runs without the profile, per-container confirmation ensures every container actually inherits the profile.

remediation.desc: Start containers without `--security-opt apparmor=unconfined`, the default profile applies automatically when AppArmor is enabled.

finding_info.title: Ensure podman containers root filesystem is mounted as read-only
finding_info.desc: Read-only root filesystems prevent attackers from writing malicious binaries, modifying system files, or tampering with container contents after compromise. Forces explicit volume mounts for writable data, improving security posture and making containers more immutable.

remediation.desc: Start containers with `--read-only` flag, or set `"ReadonlyRootfs": true` in container config. Use `--tmpfs` or named volumes for directories that need write access.

finding_info.title: Ensure Secure Boot is enabled
finding_info.desc: Secure Boot verifies that only trusted code runs during startup, preventing malware from loading before your OS starts and gaining deep system control.

remediation.desc: Follow your distribution documentation to setup Secure Boot.

finding_info.title: Ensure automatic logout from shells is configured
finding_info.desc:
Avoid leaving opened shells, potentially with elevated permissions. Set readonly "TMOUT" shell variable in "/etc/profile.d/timeout.sh": "
TMOUT=900
readonly TMOUT
export TMOUT"

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "fingerprinthash SHA256"
finding_info.desc: SHA-256 host-key fingerprints are collision-resistant and fit on one terminal line, unlike MD5. Using a weak hash risks accepting a forged fingerprint during first-connect trust-on-first-use.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "syslogfacility AUTH"
finding_info.desc: Routing sshd logs to the AUTH facility keeps authentication events alongside PAM, sudo, and su in the same log stream, simplifying correlation in SIEM rules and incident-response queries. Only useful if you are collecting logs via syslog.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "loglevel VERBOSE"
finding_info.desc: VERBOSE logging records the fingerprint of every key used to authenticate, turning silent key compromises into detectable events and providing forensic evidence for incident response.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "logingracetime" <= 60
finding_info.desc: A long LoginGraceTime lets an attacker hold open many half-finished auth attempts that consume sshd connection slots, enabling slow-DoS or password-spray campaigns. 60s is enough for legitimate logins. Increase on very slow connection if you timeout.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "permitrootlogin no"
finding_info.desc: Direct SSH login as root collapses two security barriers into one: an attacker who phishes or cracks the root password gets immediate full control with no intermediate user account, and audit logs cannot attribute the action to a specific user. Requires an alternative out-of-band access method (e.g. console, serial) for emergency root access.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "strictmodes yes"
finding_info.desc: StrictModes makes sshd refuse to read authorized_keys/.ssh files that are world- or group-writable. Without it, an attacker who gains any write access to a user's home dir can append a key to authorized_keys and gain persistent SSH login.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "maxauthtries" <= 4
finding_info.desc: Capping authentication attempts per TCP connection, increasing the protection against brute-force attacks.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "maxsessions" <= 5
finding_info.desc: Limiting multiplexed sessions per connection caps the damage from a single stolen socket: an attacker who hijacks one authenticated channel cannot fan out to dozens of shells, exec channels, or port forwards. Users relying on SSH multiplexing (e.g. ControlMaster) to run many parallel sessions (CI/CD pipelines, mass deployments) may hit the limit.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "hostbasedauthentication no"
finding_info.desc: HostbasedAuthentication trusts the client host's identity rather than a user credential, an attacker who compromises any trusted client can hop into the server as any user without further authentication.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "ignoreuserknownhosts yes"
finding_info.desc: IgnoreUserKnownHosts forces sshd to trust only the system-wide known_hosts during host-based authentication, preventing a user from whitelisting a rogue host and bypassing the admin's trust anchors. Even if host-based authentication is disable this is a better default in case it ever is.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "pubkeyauthentication yes"
finding_info.desc: Requiring public-key authentication eliminates password-based logins, blocking online brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks that exploit weak or reused passwords.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "passwordauthentication no"
finding_info.desc: Use key authentication instead of password based.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "kbdinteractiveauthentication no"
finding_info.desc: Keyboard-interactive authentication can fall back to PAM password prompts, re-opening the exact brute-force path that public-key-only mode is meant to close. Disable it unless a specific PAM two-factor module requires it.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "permitemptypasswords no"
finding_info.desc: PermitEmptyPasswords yes lets accounts with empty password fields log in over SSH with no password. Use as security in depth if password authentication must be enabled.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "kerberosauthentication no"
finding_info.desc: Unless the host is on a Kerberos realm, KerberosAuthentication just adds attack surface and a parser exposed to network input. Disabling it removes that surface entirely.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "kerberosorlocalpasswd no"
finding_info.desc: KerberosOrLocalPasswd yes lets sshd silently fall back to "/etc/passwd-style" authentication when Kerberos fails, defeating the intent to require Kerberos and re-exposing local password attacks. Defence-in-depth in case Kerberos is used.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "kerberosticketcleanup yes"
finding_info.desc: Without ticket cleanup, Kerberos credentials linger after the SSH session ends, a later attacker who reaches the host can reuse them to access other Kerberized services as the ticket's principal. Defence-in-depth in case Kerberos is used.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "gssapiauthentication no"
finding_info.desc: GSSAPI exposes additional code and parsers to remote attackers before authentication completes, on hosts not on a GSSAPI/Kerberos realm it is pure attack surface.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "gssapicleanupcredentials yes"
finding_info.desc: Leftover GSSAPI credentials after a session ends are reusable by anyone who later reaches the host as that user. Security in depth in case Kerberos is used.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "usepam yes"
finding_info.desc: "UsePAM yes" routes sshd through PAM, picking up account-lockout, faillock, lecturing, and other PAM-stack hardening. Without it, those controls are bypassed entirely on the SSH path.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "disableforwarding yes"
finding_info.desc: DisableForwarding blocks all forwarding types (tunnel, agent, X11) in one switch. An attacker with a shell cannot pivot through the SSH session to reach internal services or expose the agent socket.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "x11forwarding no"
finding_info.desc: X11 forwarding exposes the X server to the remote host, which can inject keystrokes, capture screenshots, or exploit X11 vulnerabilities. Disable it unless graphical applications are required.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "gatewayports no"
finding_info.desc: GatewayPorts allows remote hosts to connect to ports forwarded for the user, turning the SSH server into an open relay. Attackers can expose internal services to the network.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "x11uselocalhost yes"
finding_info.desc: Binding forwarded X11 displays to localhost-only prevents remote hosts from connecting to the X socket. Without it, any host that can reach the server can grab the X session.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "printmotd no"
finding_info.desc: The message-of-the-day can reveal OS version, hostname, or infrastructure details useful for targeting. Disable it if PAM already prints a vetted banner, to avoid leaking information.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "permituserenvironment no"
finding_info.desc: PermitUserEnvironment lets users set arbitrary environment variables via ~/.ssh/environment, including LD_PRELOAD to hijack libraries loaded by sshd child processes. This bypasses env_reset and other sshd security controls.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "clientaliveinterval" <= 15
finding_info.desc: ClientAliveInterval sends encrypted keep-alives at this interval. Setting it to 15s or less ensures dead or hijacked sessions are reaped quickly, reducing the window for session hijacking.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "clientalivecountmax 3"
finding_info.desc: Together with ClientAliveInterval, this caps how many missed keepalives a session can survive before sshd terminates it, closing dead sessions denies attackers a parked authenticated channel to reuse.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "tcpkeepalive no"
finding_info.desc: TCPKeepAlive sends unencrypted keep-alives that can be spoofed, making sshd believe a dead connection is still alive. Disable it and rely on ClientAliveInterval for encrypted keep-alives instead.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "usedns no"
finding_info.desc: UseDNS triggers reverse-DNS lookups on every connection, leaking client IPs to the configured resolver and adding latency. Disable it unless hostnames are required in logs.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "permittunnel no"
finding_info.desc: Prevent SSH session from creating a tun/tap device, making it a bit harder for an attacker to bridge networks. Breaks SSH VPN tunneling (ssh -w) for users who rely on it for secure remote network access.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "maxstartups 10:30:60"
finding_info.desc: MaxStartups rate-limits unauthenticated connections: after 10 pending, new connections are dropped with 30% probability, rising to 100% at 60 pending. This thwarts connection-slurping DoS and slows password-spray campaigns. Legitimate bulk SSH connections (CI/CD, mass deployments) may be dropped during peak auth times; increase the threshold on busy bastion hosts.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "printlastlog yes"
finding_info.desc: Could help detect an unauthorized connection if the last login is not recognized.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "allowgroups sshusers"
finding_info.desc: SSH access should be restricted to a group of users. Users not in the specified group will be denied SSH access, including system administrators not added to the group.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "kexalgorithms mlkem768x25519-sha256,sntrup761x25519-sha512,sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com,curve25519-sha256,curve25519-sha256@libssh.org,ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521"
finding_info.desc: Pinning key-exchange algorithms to a vetted modern set blocks downgrade to weak/legacy KEX (e.g. SHA-1-based DH groups) and includes post-quantum hybrids (mlkem, sntrup) so today's recorded sessions cannot be decrypted by future quantum-capable adversaries. Older SSH clients that only support legacy algorithms will be unable to connect.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "ciphers chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com,aes128-gcm@openssh.com,aes256-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes128-ctr"
finding_info.desc: Pinning ciphers to authenticated-encryption (AEAD) and CTR-with-MAC modes blocks downgrade to CBC, RC4, and 3DES, historically broken to recover plaintext from captured SSH traffic. Older SSH clients that only support legacy ciphers will be unable to connect.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "macs hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256,umac-128@openssh.com"
finding_info.desc: Pinning MACs to encrypt-then-MAC (ETM) SHA-2 family blocks the historically-broken MD5/SHA-1 MACs and the encrypt-and-MAC ordering that has produced timing oracles in OpenSSH. Older SSH clients that only support legacy MACs will be unable to connect.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "authenticationmethods publickey"
finding_info.desc: Enforces the use of publickey for authentication, eliminating fall-back paths to credential auth.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sshd is configured with "subsystem sftp /usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server -f AUTHPRIV -l INFO"
finding_info.desc: Configure SFTP to log to AUTHPRIV at INFO, every file transfer over SFTP appears in the auth log, turning otherwise-silent file exfil over SSH into something that can be detected and audited.

finding_info.title: Ensure sshd service file is owned by root
finding_info.desc: If a non-root user owns the sshd systemd unit file, they can edit it and have that wrapper run as root the next time sshd is started, would allow for full local privilege escalation.

finding_info.title: Ensure sshd service file permissions 644 are set
finding_info.desc: If a non-root user as permissions on the sshd systemd unit file, they can edit it and have that wrapper run as root the next time sshd is started, would allow for full local privilege escalation.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/ssh" directory is owned by root
finding_info.desc: /etc/ssh holds host private keys and sshd_config, non-root ownership lets that user steal host keys or rewrite sshd_config to weaken the security policy.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/ssh" directory permissions is 755
finding_info.desc: /etc/ssh holds host private keys and sshd_config, open permissions lets users steal host keys or rewrite sshd_config to weaken the security policy.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/ssh/sshd_config" file is owned by root
finding_info.desc: Could allow an attacker to reconfigure sshd.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/ssh/sshd_config" file permissions is 644 or stricter
finding_info.desc: Could allow an attacker to reconfigure sshd.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/" directory is owned by root
finding_info.desc: Could allow an attacker to reconfigure sshd.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/" files are owned by root
finding_info.desc: Could allow an attacker to reconfigure sshd.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/" files permissions are 644 or stricter
finding_info.desc: Could allow an attacker to reconfigure sshd.

findings.message: file "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-cloudimg-settings.conf" permission: wanted "644" or stricter got "666"

finding_info.title: Ensure SSH private host key files have permissions 600
finding_info.desc: SSH private host keys must have restrictive permissions. If they are world-readable, an attacker can steal them and impersonate the server, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.

finding_info.title: Ensure SSH public host key files have permissions 644
finding_info.desc: SSH public host keys should have correct permissions. Overly permissive public keys could be tampered with, leading to trust-on-first-use poisoning.

finding_info.title: Ensure SSH host key files are owned by root
finding_info.desc: SSH host key files must be owned by root to prevent unauthorized users from modifying them. Non-root ownership could allow an attacker to replace host keys and impersonate the server.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "noexec" is set
finding_info.desc: Prevent commands run via sudo from spawning further processes (blocks shell escapes from editors/pagers that link against the preloaded dummy exec(3) wrappers). Breaks legitimate commands that need to spawn subprocesses (e.g. running a shell, executing scripts that fork, some CI/CD tooling).

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "requiretty" is set
finding_info.desc: Refuse to run unless sudo is invoked from a real tty, blocking exploitation paths via cron jobs or web shells. This slows down attacks but does not completely prevent them, just makes it a bit harder. May break remote management tools, can be ignored for a remote management user with: "Defaults:user !noexec".

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "use_pty" is set
finding_info.desc: Run the target command in a new pseudo-terminal so a compromised child cannot inject input into the parent tty.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "umask=0027" is set
finding_info.desc: Force a restrictive umask on files created by sudo'd commands. Files created with sudo will have restrictive permissions (no access for others); may break scripts or workflows that expect world-readable files.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "ignore_dot" is set
finding_info.desc: Skip "." when searching PATH for the target binary. Without it, an attacker who drops a malicious binary into a sudo'd user's CWD can have it executed as root simply because PATH started with ".".

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "passwd_timeout=1" is set
finding_info.desc: Abort the password prompt after 1 minute idle.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "env_reset" is set
finding_info.desc: Start the command with a minimal, sanitized environment (only variables on env_keep survive), blocks LD_PRELOAD-style attacks. Breaks scripts and applications that depend on user environment variables (e.g. PATH customizations, application-specific env vars) unless explicitly added to env_keep.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "timestamp_timeout=0" is set
finding_info.desc: Never cache credentials, every sudo invocation re-prompts for the password.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "mail_badpass" is set
finding_info.desc: Send mail to the sudo mailto address whenever a user enters an incorrect password at the sudo prompt.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "logfile="/var/log/sudo.log"" is set
finding_info.desc: Append a record of every sudo command (success and failure) to this file in addition to syslog.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "lecture="always"" is set
finding_info.desc: The sudo lecture warns users about the responsibilities and risks of elevated privileges before every invocation. Always-on mode ensures the warning is never silently skipped.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudo default config "lecture_file="/usr/share/doc/sudo_lecture.txt"" is set
finding_info.desc: Point the sudo lecture at an organization-specific text so every sudo invocation reminds users of local policy instead of the default generic warning.

remediation.desc: In "/etc/sudoers" or "/etc/sudoers.d/*" add: "Defaults lecture_file="/usr/share/doc/sudo_lecture.txt"" and provide that file with the org's warning text.

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudoers config does not contain "NOPASSWD"
finding_info.desc: "NOPASSWD" lets a sudo-able account escalate to root with no password prompt at all. An attacker who steals only the user's session token (no password) immediately becomes root. Defeats the whole point of sudo's auth gate.

findings.message: test ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL, ubuntu ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL

remediation.desc: In "/etc/sudoers" and "/etc/sudoers.d/*" remove all instances with "NOPASSWD"

finding_info.title: Ensure that sudoers re authentication is not disabled
finding_info.desc: "!authenticate" disables the password prompt entirely for matching rules, the same effect as "NOPASSWD" via the negated tag form, often missed by NOPASSWD-only audits. Removes the auth gate that protects every sudo invocation.

remediation.desc: In "/etc/sudoers" and "/etc/sudoers.d/*" remove all instances with "!authenticate"

finding_info.title: Ensure sudoers config file permissions is 440
finding_info.desc: Looser permissions on "/etc/sudoers" let unauthorized users read or modify the privilege policy: reading reveals exploitable rules, writing grants instant root via a self-added "NOPASSWD ALL" line.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/sudoers config file is owned by root
finding_info.desc: If "/etc/sudoers" is owned by a non-root user, that user can edit the privilege policy and grant themselves root.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/sudoers.d/ files permissions are 440
finding_info.desc: Looser permissions on "/etc/sudoers.d/" let unauthorized users read or modify the privilege policy: reading reveals exploitable rules, writing grants instant root via a self-added "NOPASSWD ALL" line.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/sudoers.d/ files are owned by root
finding_info.desc: If "/etc/sudoers.d/" is owned by a non-root user, that user can edit the privilege policy and grant themselves root.

finding_info.title: Ensure audit rule for sudo log file is present
finding_info.desc: Monitoring the sudo log file for writes and attribute changes detects attempts to tamper with privilege escalation records.

remediation.desc: Add "-w /var/log/sudo.log -p wa -k log_file" to a file under "/etc/audit/rules.d/" and "augenrules --load".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.kptr_restrict" = 2
finding_info.desc: Restrict kernel address visibility via /proc and other interfaces, regardless of user privileges, kernel pointers expose specific locations in kernel memory, will hide kernel symbol addresses in /proc/kallsyms.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.kptr_restrict = 2" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.ftrace_enabled" = 0
finding_info.desc: Disable ftrace debugging. Ftrace provides tracing facilities for the kernel that can expose sensitive information. Disabling it breaks kernel tracing and profiling tools (e.g. perf, bpftrace) that rely on ftrace.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.ftrace_enabled = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.randomize_va_space" = 2
finding_info.desc: Enable ASLR for mmap base, stack, VDSO pages, and heap. Forces shared libraries to be loaded at random addresses. May cause breakages with legacy applications.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.randomize_va_space = 2" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.dmesg_restrict" = 1
finding_info.desc: Restrict access to the kernel log buffer to users with CAP_SYSLOG. Kernel logs often contain sensitive information such as kernel pointers. Non-root users and scripts that read dmesg will no longer work.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.dmesg_restrict = 1" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.printk" = "3\t3\t3\t3"
finding_info.desc: Prevent kernel information leaks in the console during boot. Must be used in conjunction with kernel boot parameters.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.printk = 3	3	3	3" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.perf_cpu_time_max_percent" = 1
finding_info.desc: Cap perf CPU usage. Without a low cap, perf and perf-based tracing/profiling can consume excessive CPU on busy systems, increasing attack surface for DoS via heavy tracing workloads.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.perf_cpu_time_max_percent = 1" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.perf_event_max_sample_rate" = 1
finding_info.desc: Cap perf sample rate. Uncapped rates produce timing oracles and let unprivileged perf users dominate the perf subsystem, slowing security-relevant workloads.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.perf_event_max_sample_rate = 1" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.perf_event_paranoid" = 2 or 3
finding_info.desc: Restrict kernel profiling to users with CAP_PERFMON. The performance events system should not be accessible by unprivileged users, as it adds considerable kernel attack surface. Can be 2 or 3.

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.sysrq" = 0
finding_info.desc: Disable the SysRq magic keys. From the physical console, or from /proc/sysrq-trigger as root, they otherwise allow kernel memory and task dumps, forced remounts, syncs and reboots, leaking kernel information and disrupting availability. The Secure Attention Key (SAK) can no longer be utilized.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.sysrq = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.kexec_load_disabled" = 1
finding_info.desc: Disable kexec. Kexec can be used to replace the running kernel, which is only useful for live kernel patching without rebooting.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.kexec_load_disabled = 1" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled" = 1 or 2
finding_info.desc: Restrict the bpf() syscall to users with CAP_BPF, unprivileged BPF is a major local privilege escalation surface. Can be 1 or 2, where 2 makes the restriction permanent until reboot. Breaks unprivileged BPF programs (e.g. rootless containers, network monitoring tools), leave it to 0 if using rootless containers.

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.panic_on_oops" = 1
finding_info.desc: Force the kernel to panic on oopses. This can potentially indicate and thwart certain kernel exploitation attempts, and also causes panics on machine check exceptions. Some bad drivers can cause harmless oopses which result in system crash.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.panic_on_oops = 1" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.panic" = "-1"
finding_info.desc: Reboot immediately on kernel panic. A panic could indicate an exploitation attempt. Appropriate for security-critical hosts where the safe response to a corruption-detected event is reboot, not stay-up.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.panic = -1" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "kernel.modules_disabled" = 1
finding_info.desc: Permanently disable module loading once set. Any later attempt by an attacker, even with CAP_SYS_MODULE and root, to load a module is rejected by the kernel. This could prevent loading backdoor or vulnerable modules. For systems needing hot-add drivers, it prevents legitimate module loading.

remediation.desc: Add "kernel.modules_disabled = 1" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".
