finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.icmp.ratelimit" >= 1 and <= 100
finding_info.desc: ICMPv6 twin of SYN_064: rate-limit outgoing ICMPv6 errors to block rate side channels and slow reconnaissance. Kernel default 100. Must be non-zero, 0 disables the rate limiting entirely.

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.icmp.ratelimit = 100" (any value between 1 and 100) in "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf" and run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.icmp.ratemask" = "0-1,3-127"
finding_info.desc: ICMPv6 types covered by ratelimit, a range list (not the IPv4 bitmask). Default 0-1,3-127 covers all types except Packet Too Big (type 2, needed for PMTUD).

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.icmp.ratemask = 0-1,3-127" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.max_dst_opts_number" <= 8
finding_info.desc: Cap destination options per packet. Unlimited options are a parsing-DoS and IDS-evasion vector.

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.max_dst_opts_number = 8" (or lower) in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.max_hbh_opts_number" <= 8
finding_info.desc: Cap hop-by-hop options per packet. HBH headers are processed by every router on the path (amplified DoS).

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.max_hbh_opts_number = 8" (or lower) in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.max_dst_opts_length" <= 65536
finding_info.desc: Cap total destination-options length. The INT_MAX default allows huge option blobs to burn CPU.

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.max_dst_opts_length = 65536" (or lower) in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.max_hbh_length" <= 65536
finding_info.desc: Cap total hop-by-hop-options length. The INT_MAX default allows huge option blobs to burn CPU.

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.max_hbh_length = 65536" (or lower) in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.ip6frag_time" <= 15
finding_info.desc: Shrink the IPv6 fragment reassembly window (default 60). Fragments are a DoS and IDS-evasion vehicle, shorter retention limits both.

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.ip6frag_time = 15" (or lower) in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.ip6frag_high_thresh" <= 4194304
finding_info.desc: Cap memory held for IPv6 fragment reassembly. Beyond it fragments are dropped instead of exhausting RAM.

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.ip6frag_high_thresh = 4194304" (or lower) in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.conf.all.seg6_enabled" = 0
finding_info.desc: Keep SRv6 (segment routing) disabled. Every enabled extension-header routing mode is additional parser attack surface.

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.conf.all.seg6_enabled = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.conf.default.seg6_enabled" = 0
finding_info.desc: Keep SRv6 (segment routing) disabled by default. Every enabled extension-header routing mode is additional parser attack surface.

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.conf.default.seg6_enabled = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.conf.all.rpl_seg_enabled" = 0
finding_info.desc: Keep RPL source routing disabled (same rationale as seg6_enabled).

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.conf.all.rpl_seg_enabled = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.conf.default.rpl_seg_enabled" = 0
finding_info.desc: Keep RPL source routing disabled by default (same rationale as seg6_enabled).

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.conf.default.rpl_seg_enabled = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.conf.all.ioam6_enabled" = 0
finding_info.desc: Keep in-situ OAM disabled (same rationale as seg6_enabled).

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.conf.all.ioam6_enabled = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.ipv6.conf.default.ioam6_enabled" = 0
finding_info.desc: Keep in-situ OAM disabled by default (same rationale as seg6_enabled).

remediation.desc: Add "net.ipv6.conf.default.ioam6_enabled = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal" = 0
finding_info.desc: Keep strict TCP window tracking. Out-of-window segments are marked INVALID and dropped by policy firewalls (blind RST/SYN-injection hardening). 1 accepts them, weakening stateful filtering.

remediation.desc: Add "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_ignore_invalid_rst" = 0
finding_info.desc: Keep marking out-of-window RSTs INVALID (default). Combined with an INVALID-drop rule this defeats blind RST teardown of tracked connections.

remediation.desc: Add "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_ignore_invalid_rst = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_loose" = 0
finding_info.desc: Do not pick up mid-stream connections as ESTABLISHED. Strict mode forces every connection through NEW-state rules. Breaks asymmetric routing and firewall failover.

remediation.desc: Add "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_loose = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_checksum" = 1
finding_info.desc: Keep L4 checksum verification of incoming packets. Corrupt packets become INVALID instead of being tracked. Small CPU cost, mostly moot with NIC checksum offload.

remediation.desc: Add "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_checksum = 1" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_log_invalid" = 0
finding_info.desc: Detection option: log INVALID packets per protocol (255 = any). Very noisy under scan/attack, keep off by default.

remediation.desc: Add "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_log_invalid = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.netfilter.nf_hooks_lwtunnel" = 0
finding_info.desc: One-way switch (cannot be disabled once enabled). Leave off unless lightweight-tunnel netfilter hooks are required.

remediation.desc: Add "net.netfilter.nf_hooks_lwtunnel = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure sysctl "net.mptcp.enabled" = 0
finding_info.desc: MPTCP is enabled by default on Ubuntu. An unused second TCP stack is pure attack surface with a steady CVE history. Alternatively blacklist the mptcp module.

remediation.desc: Add "net.mptcp.enabled = 0" in a sysctl config file "/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf". Then run "sysctl --system".

finding_info.title: Ensure no reboot is required
finding_info.desc: A pending reboot indicates that security updates have been installed but are not yet active, leaving the system potentially vulnerable.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/hostname is owned by root
finding_info.desc: The hostname file should be owned by root to prevent unauthorized modification of the system hostname, which could affect network identification and log attribution.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/hostname has permissions 644
finding_info.desc: The hostname file should have appropriate permissions to prevent unauthorized modification.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/machine-id is owned by root
finding_info.desc: The machine-id file should be owned by root. Tampering with machine-id can break logging, licensing, and other system identification mechanisms.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/machine-id has permissions 444
finding_info.desc: The machine-id should be read-only to prevent unauthorized changes. Some systems may not have this file.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/hosts file is owned by root
finding_info.desc: The /etc/hosts file controls hostname resolution. Non-root ownership could allow an attacker to redirect traffic by modifying DNS entries, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/hosts file has permissions 644
finding_info.desc: The /etc/hosts file should have restrictive permissions to prevent unauthorized modification of hostname resolution, which could redirect traffic to malicious servers.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/resolv.conf is owned by root or systemd-resolve
finding_info.desc: The resolv.conf file controls DNS resolution. Non-root ownership could allow an attacker to redirect DNS queries to malicious servers. When systemd-resolved manages DNS, ownership by systemd-resolve:systemd-resolve is also acceptable.

remediation.desc: chown root:root /etc/resolv.conf (or leave as systemd-resolve:systemd-resolve if using systemd-resolved)

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/resolv.conf has permissions 644
finding_info.desc: The resolv.conf file should have restrictive permissions to prevent unauthorized modification of DNS configuration.

finding_info.title: Ensure that systemd config "CtrlAltDelBurstAction=none"
finding_info.desc: Disables the ability to rapidly trigger system reboots, protecting against accidental or malicious reboot attempts.

finding_info.title: Ensure /etc/systemd/system/ files permissions are owned by root
finding_info.desc: A unprotected systemd system service file could lead to privilege escalation.

finding_info.title: Ensure uptime is no more than 3 months
finding_info.desc: Long-running systems may be missing critical kernel and security patches that require a reboot to take effect.

finding_info.title: Ensure that root is the only user with UID 0
finding_info.desc: Multiple accounts with UID 0 are root-equivalent for filesystem and process semantics. An attacker who creates one bypasses every name-based audit and detection that watches the literal "root" user.

remediation.desc: Identify the offending account in "/etc/passwd" and either delete it or assign it a fresh non-zero UID. Investigate how it was created.

finding_info.title: Ensure no duplicate user names exist
finding_info.desc: Duplicate user names indicate hand-edited passwd or merged user databases. Tools may resolve only the first match, masking permissions and audit attribution on the shadowed entry.

remediation.desc: Edit "/etc/passwd" to remove or rename the duplicate. Investigate the source.

finding_info.title: Ensure no duplicate UIDs exist
finding_info.desc: Two user names sharing one UID makes ownership and audit logs ambiguous: a file owned by UID X cannot be reliably attributed to one principal, undermining accountability and forensics.

remediation.desc: Renumber duplicates via "usermod -u <new-uid> <name>" and "chown -R" their files. Investigate the duplicate's origin.

finding_info.title: Ensure that "/etc/securetty" is empty
finding_info.desc: An empty (or missing) "/etc/securetty" disables direct root login on every console, physical and virtual, forcing administrators to log in as themselves and sudo to root, which preserves audit attribution.

remediation.desc: Truncate the file or remove it.

finding_info.title: Ensure no login is available on system accounts
finding_info.desc: System accounts (UID < 1000) own daemons, not humans, granting them an interactive shell turns each one into a possible login target.

finding_info.title: Ensure all passwords are hashed with yescrypt
finding_info.desc: Hashes from older algorithms (DES, MD5, SHA-256/512 crypt) are far cheaper to crack on modern GPUs than yescrypt (which also requires RAM to crack/calculate).

remediation.desc: Edit PAM passwd to use yescrypt when changing password, and force users to change passwords "passwd --expire <user>".

finding_info.title: Ensure no accounts are locked, delete them
finding_info.desc: Locked accounts that are kept around clutter the user database and risk being unlocked accidentally. If an account is no longer needed, deletion is cleaner than indefinite locking.

remediation.desc: After confirming the account is not needed: "userdel -r <name>". Investigate any locked account whose home dir still contains active data before deleting.

finding_info.title: Ensure that all home directories exist
finding_info.desc: A missing home directory referenced from "/etc/passwd" could be created by an attacker, and could include configurations that could lead to privilege escalation or persistence.

remediation.desc: Either re-create the missing directory with the right ownership and 0700 permissions, or remove the user with "userdel".

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/shadow" password fields are not empty
finding_info.desc: An empty password field in "/etc/shadow" lets that account log in with no password at all, on any service that consults shadow (login, ssh PasswordAuthentication, etc.).

remediation.desc: Lock the account immediately: "passwd -l <name>"; then either set a real password "passwd <name>" or delete the account.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/passwd" password fields are not empty
finding_info.desc: An empty password field, instead of "x" in "/etc/passwd", means the system reads the password directly from passwd and treats absence as no password required.

remediation.desc: Run "pwconv" to migrate password fields to "/etc/shadow", investigate any user with an empty field.

finding_info.title: Ensure accounts in "/etc/passwd" use shadowed passwords
finding_info.desc: Password hashes in "/etc/passwd" are world-readable, exposing every account's hash to any local user for cracking.

remediation.desc: Run "pwconv" to migrate hashes to "/etc/shadow", verify all password fields in "/etc/passwd" are "x".

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/passwd" file permissions are "644"
finding_info.desc: Looser permissions on "/etc/passwd" let unprivileged users edit account metadata (UID, shell, home dir) and grant themselves access, tighter than 0644 breaks userland tools that need to resolve user names.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/passwd" file owner is "root:root" or file is missing
finding_info.desc: If "/etc/passwd" is owned by a non-root user, that user can edit account UIDs and shells, granting themselves UID 0 or pointing root's shell at malicious code.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/shadow" file owner is correct
finding_info.desc: Wrong ownership on "/etc/shadow" lets a non-root principal read every account's password hash for offline cracking, or rewrite hashes to take over arbitrary accounts.

remediation.desc:
On Debian: "chown root:shadow /etc/shadow"
On other distros: "chown root:root /etc/shadow"

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/shadow" file permissions are correct
finding_info.desc: Loose permissions on "/etc/shadow" expose every account's password hash to non-root users, who can then crack them.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/shadow-" file owner is correct or file is missing
finding_info.desc: "/etc/shadow-" is the previous-generation backup of shadow, if its ownership is wrong, an attacker can recover password hashes from the backup that the live file's tighter ownership would have blocked.

remediation.desc:
On Debian: "chown root:shadow /etc/shadow-"
On other distros: "chown root:root /etc/shadow-"

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/shadow-" file permissions are correct or file is missing
finding_info.desc: Loose permissions on the shadow backup file leak the same password hashes as the live file.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/security/opasswd" file owner is "root:root" or file is missing
finding_info.desc: "/etc/security/opasswd" stores previously-used password hashes for "pam_pwhistory" reuse prevention. Wrong ownership exposes those historical hashes to non-root users for cracking, leaking old password that could indicate patterns or be reused elsewhere.

finding_info.title: Ensure "/etc/security/opasswd" file permissions are "600" or file is missing
finding_info.desc: "/etc/security/opasswd" stores previously-used password hashes for "pam_pwhistory" reuse prevention. Wrong permissions exposes those historical hashes to non-root users for cracking, leaking old password that could indicate patterns or be reused elsewhere.

finding_info.title: Ensure no users have ".rhosts" or ".shosts" files
finding_info.desc: Legacy .rhosts files enable trust-based authentication without passwords, a major security risk. If an attacker compromises any trusted host, they can log in as any user on this system without credentials.

remediation.desc: Remove all .rhosts, .shosts files from user home directories: find /home -name ".rhosts" -delete

finding_info.title: Ensure all users' home directories are owned by their respective user
finding_info.desc: Home directories owned by other users could allow unauthorized access to files. An attacker could read private keys, configuration files, or plant malicious files.

finding_info.title: Ensure all users' home directories have permissions 750 or stricter
finding_info.desc: World-writable or world-readable home directories expose private user data to other users on the system. Permissions should be 750 or stricter to prevent unauthorized access.

finding_info.title: Ensure no users have world-writable files in their home directory
finding_info.desc: World-writable files in user home directories can be modified by any user on the system, enabling data tampering and potential privilege escalation via .bashrc, .profile, or crontab modification.

remediation.desc: Find and fix: find /home -type f -perm -0002 -exec chmod o-w {} \;

finding_info.title: Ensure root account is disabled
finding_info.desc: An enabled root account with a valid password and an interactive shell is the single highest-value target for brute-force and credential-theft attacks. Disabling it forces administrators to log in as themselves and use "sudo", which preserves non-repudiable audit trails. Ensure you have valid admin accounts.

remediation.desc: Lock the password: "passwd -l root" and set the shell to nologin: "usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin root".

finding_info.title: Ensure account is disabled when password is expired
finding_info.desc: Set the number of days after a password expires until the account is permanently disabled to instantly. Password expiry could mean that the account should rotate it's password, or that the password was compromised, in either case the account should be locked to prevent it from being used until the password is changed. Especially useful when doing mandatory password rotation, but be careful to always keep a valid access to the host.

findings.message: root, daemon, bin, sys, sync, games, man, lp, mail, news, uucp, proxy, www-data, backup, list, irc, _apt, nobody, systemd-network, systemd-timesync, dhcpcd, messagebus, syslog, systemd-resolve, uuidd, tss, sshd, pollinate, tcpdump, landscape, fwupd-refresh, polkitd, test, ubuntu, root2, nopass, ghost, expired, weakhash

finding_info.title: Ensure account is disabled when password is expired by default
finding_info.desc: Set the number of days after a password expires until the account is permanently disabled to instantly. Password expiry could mean that the account should rotate it's password, or that the password was compromised, in either case the account should be locked to prevent it from being used until the password is changed. Especially useful when doing mandatory password rotation, but be careful to always keep a valid access to the host.

remediation.desc: Edit useradd configuration in: "/etc/default/useradd" and set: "INACTIVE=0".
